label: prf:t-beta-markov-frobenius-collapse
title: Proof of t beta markov frobenius collapse
html:
Completing the square.

Let X \in H satisfy the constraint \mathrm{tr}_M(X) = S. Write the decomposition X = (X - S \cdot 1) + S \cdot 1 and expand the Frobenius norm-squared:

\| X \|^2_\tau = \mathrm{tr}_M(X X^\dagger)
              = \mathrm{tr}_M\big((X - S \cdot 1)(X - S \cdot 1)^\dagger\big)
                + S \, \mathrm{tr}_M(X + X^\dagger) - S^2 \, \mathrm{tr}_M(1).

(The scalar S \cdot 1 is central and fixed by \dagger, so (X - S \cdot 1)(X - S \cdot 1)^\dagger = X X^\dagger - S(X + X^\dagger) + S^2 \cdot 1. Since \mathrm{tr}_M(T_w) = \mathrm{tr}_M(T_{w^{-1}}), the trace is \dagger-invariant, so \mathrm{tr}_M(X^\dagger) = \mathrm{tr}_M(X) = S; applying linearity term by term gives the identity above.)

Substituting the Markov normalisation \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = 1 and the constraint \mathrm{tr}_M(X) = S:

\| X \|^2_\tau = \| X - S \cdot 1 \|^2_\tau + 2 S^2 - S^2
             = \| X - S \cdot 1 \|^2_\tau + S^2.

The twisted form is positive-semi-definite: in the orthogonal seminormal form each \sigma_i is real symmetric, so \dagger is the blockwise transpose and \| Y \|^2_\tau = \sum_\lambda y_\lambda \, \| Y_\lambda \|_F^2 \ge 0, since every Markov weight y_\lambda \ge 0. Therefore

\| X \|^2_\tau \;\ge\; S^2,

with equality iff \| X - S \cdot 1 \|^2_\tau = 0, i.e. iff X - S \cdot 1 vanishes on every block with y_\lambda > 0. At z = q^3/(q^2+1) the blocks with y_\lambda = 0 are exactly the shapes with three or more rows, so the minimiser is S \cdot 1 up to that radical. (The untwisted form \mathrm{tr}_M(X \cdot X) cannot be used: it is negative on \sigma_1\sigma_2 - \sigma_2\sigma_1 \in H_3.)

Therefore T_\beta = S \cdot 1 is a minimum-Frobenius-norm primal-feasible element, with \| T_\beta \|^2_\tau = S^2. \quad\blacksquare
